usageNotes: Use this to open a terminal proxy session to a running QEMU VM from the web UI or a terminal client; the caller must hold VM.Console on the target VM. Returns a ticket, port, and UPID — pass the ticket to the noVNC/xterm.js WebSocket handshake to authenticate the session. If the VM has a configured serial device and you need a serial console rather than the QEMU display, supply the 'serial' parameter (e.g. 'serial0').

examples.summary: Open a standard terminal proxy session to VM 101 on node pve1

tips: The returned 'ticket' is short-lived; use it immediately to establish the WebSocket connection.
Omit 'serial' to connect to the QEMU display console (default); specify 'serial0'–'serial3' only when the VM uses a serial-based console (e.g. headless Linux with console=ttyS0).
The 'upid' in the response can be polled via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status if you need to confirm the proxy process started successfully.
This endpoint requires the VM to be running; calling it against a stopped VM will return an error.
